one_liner: Coda (Superhuman Docs) has a broad REST API v1 at coda.io/apis/v1 with an OpenAPI spec, API tokens, and a vendor-published MCP server; it looks buildable now.
auth_notes: The supplied pages show only that API tokens are generated at coda.io/account (stated in the Admin API article). The pages do not describe REST API auth in detail. The MCP sign-in flow is an OAuth-style browser grant, but the supplied text does not confirm OAuth2 or PKCE. The draft's OAuth2 claim could not be verified, so it was dropped from auth_methods. Composio lists API_KEY only.
access_notes: The API docs have a 'Free and Paid Workspaces' section, but its text was truncated in the supplied pages. The draft's 'free of charge' quote could not be verified. Pages show no plan gating on the main API; only the Admin API is Enterprise-only. Self-serve free access is the most defensible value but has lower confidence.
blocker_notes: Rate limits are modest (writes 10 per 6s). The Admin API is Enterprise-only, but it is not needed for a core toolkit. The REST token flow is not fully documented in the supplied pages.

evidence.quote: The Superhuman Docs API is a RESTful API that lets you programmatically interact with data in Superhuman Docs (formerly Coda)
This API uses a base path of https://coda.io/apis/v1 .
Only [org admins](https://coda-docs.zendesk.com/hc/articles/39555906605965) on an Enterprise plan have access to Coda’s Admin API.
you can generate an API token at [https://coda.io/account](https://coda.io/account) to use for these endpoints.
you may also want to consider using the Superhuman Docs MCP server
The **Coda MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is a connection layer that enables AI clients - like Cursor, Claude, etc. - to read and write to your Coda docs using plain-language prompts.
